surfaces.part: stone cliff wall with dark crack lines
dark foliage and water at the base

answer.evidence: The drawing is a full-width vertical cliff face with crack lines, a waterfall and foliage at the bottom, 64 rows tall and 16 px wide. Every row is a vertical face. No band at the top ends in a front-edge line followed by eave shadow, there is no ellipse, and there is no roof or canopy plane. Row 0 is only a dark outline row. The light rows near 29-32 are a white water lip, not a horizontal surface seen from above. The object is a cliff wall rather than a gate, pavilion or building, and it shows no top surface at all.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate on the right of the magenta bar is a tiny narrow strip, not a building. It shows a grey stone chasm wall with a small icicle or white drip and a dark green clump at the bottom. It has no roof, walls, door or windows, so it does not match the building kind (roof + walls + door/windows). Measured facts: 12 visible tones per tile is on par with the references (12 and 10), and near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. But 86% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 7% and 9% for the references, which points to a neutral black/grey outline rather than the dark material-tone outlines Beodeul uses. Shading on the stone is shallow, about 3-4 steps against the references' 5-6 per material (tile roof ramps, per-stone shading). The piece cannot be compared fairly as a building, and the neutral outline is the sticker look, so it fails.
